data: Great game with an interesting story, Highly recommend
beautiful game with an amazing storyline and design :) highly recommend for those who like cozy games
A great game with great artwork, calming music, great characters and stories with fun gameplay, overall a really good game imo
the art is amazing, gameplay amazing, characters amazing- truly one of the best games i've ever played
so cute and fun gameplay, lots of content to explore i love this game
The quests and dialogues are very repetitive and boring, and the game cycle is just not it
Sadly the gameplay is horrible, dull and I'm unable to force myself to play more
the rest is just a mess of repetitive, boring and unpolished minigames
there is nothing worse than getting to meet all these lovely spirits, especially my beautiful boy Stanley, and remembering this is a game about death and i have to let them all go eventually..

This game came to me at the right time in my life for it to really hit home. I'm currently living with my very old and rapidly aging grandparents. Death is always on my mind.

I was really doubting whether or not I would enjoy it for the first few hours. Then I said goodbye to Gwen and knew I had to finish it. The gameplay can be a bit drab and repetitive at times. It was for me, at first, but I grew to enjoy the simple labors and work that went into caring for these spirits. I found each of them charming in their own way and every farewell was an event I dedicated the whole of my attention to.

I cried. A lot. And I'm grateful for that. Thank you for the wonderful game. Thank you for the reminder that goodbyes can be beautiful.

This game was very cute and has a very interesting view on what can happen after death. The story and art style are 10/10 and I played all the way through twice and got all achievements. This is a nice and calm game to play if you just want to relax.

Spirtfarer is a quirky management game; you can build a boat, explore, farm, mine, fish, harvest, cook, and generally craft while befriending recently deceased spirits and caring for them before releasing them into the afterlife.

While you care for them, you will learn the various spirits' engaging and often poignant backstories. You'll find that you relate to and like some characters and not others.

It's generally a chill and relaxing adventure where you can't make mistakes, and the controls are super easy to learn.

I played this in a local co-op with my 10yr old daughter despite 'death' being the game's primary theme. However, 'death' is treated so thoughtfully and respectfully that I wouldn't hesitate to recommend playing with kids younger than the official rating of 'teens' or '12 and up' (depending on your region).

This game is one of the more unique bits of media I've even consumed.

Recommended!

I wish I could give a positive review.

I like the story and the base idea.

but due to photosensitivity, it is very painful to play. Further, I would like to note, that there are no disclosures about flashing lights in the game or on the store page. When I researched about the matter, I read that it's apparently disclosed in the faq, but I haven't found the faq myself to confirm.
While I don't have epilepsy, luckily, I can see how this game could harm my friends who do have epilepsy.
it is no less but neglectful to know that your game causes issues with people who have issues with photosensitvity and epilepsy and STILL decide to not disclose it anywhere. Furthermore, in the steam forums I have researched in, the devs appear to be aware of the issue, but insist that it's epilepsy safe, while people complain within the VERY SAME FORUM about epileptic reactions and other issues.
That neglect has the potential to kill someone.

If you can't change the game, at least put up a warning. Keep people safe, if your game is unsafe. Do better, please.

The minigames and tasks within the game also tend to become very repetitive over time, but in regards to the photosensitivity issue, this is a nothingburger.

There's a lot of heart in this little gem.

From the style, to the individual stories of the spirits. From the animations, to the care in which it handles a wide variety of different topics. And most importantly, it doesn't force you to care, it really wants you to. You will help that hedgehog day after day not because you have to, but because you feel it's the right thing to do.

It's the kind of game that made me forge a new word. "Pretty cry". The opposite of Ugly cry. And it's an antitode to the awfulness of the world we live in.

Give it a chance.

This is the 2nd place in my must-play game lists (The winner is Disco Elysium). I love story-rich game play, and this one nail it! I love the story line that focus on human life; complicated feeling, inner child, trauma, death, etc. The game play is also wonderful. The semi-open world provides possibilities to choose your own story line or your path. There are variety of mini games and puzzles to solve. How can I say! this game is a harmony combination of adventure, survival, story-rich, and management games.
This game is absolutely amazing. Very cozy and not competitive but I love it and reccomend it to everyone around me. 10/10 sooooo worth it

One of the most beautifully written and heartfelt games I've played. This entry in the cozy genre addresses the topics of death and grieving in a direct and poetic manner. The pace is slow, as it should be, to allow you to develop a real connection with the spirits aboard your vessel as you ferry them through their final reflections. Each journey to the Everdoor brought such emotion and I can say confidently that no game has made me cry as much as this one, and it felt SO good. The gameplay fairly easy but it doesn't feel shallow at all. Also, the music is so good I play the soundtrack often when I'm working. The layers of story are complex - it's easy to miss the many symbolic details but when you do catch them they tug at your heartstrings all the more for it. I truly love this game and rank it as one of my all times favorites. A true work of narrative and visual art. I highly recommend Spiritfarer - and a nice box of tissues to go with it. (not the cheap kind either, get the name brand. You'll need it.)

This game was so beautifully made. I love the art. The gameplay was amazing, I couldn't put this game down until I finished it. The story grips you and has so many aspects that I feel like will feel relatable and makes you think about the times you have had to let someone go, or have someone approaching their time. After playing this game you will want to hug your loved ones, it makes you want to not take a single moment for granted.

I have played this game multiple times and I know for a fact I will continue to come back. The music, the characters, the scenery, and the storyline are all the most beautiful I have ever seen in a game. This is my most favorite game and probably always will be!

This is an ultimate cozy game. Its very wholesome, while still touching important and hard topics for folks. As someone who works in the mental health domain, I think this game does a great job of portraying what real grief, trauma, struggles, friendships and most importantly healing looks like. I really enjoy crafting, so the differing "mini-game" tasks for crafting really made me happy. I also enjoyed figuring out ways to maximize the usage of the space on my ship and the base management aspects. I have not finished the game, but I am planning on playing the game to completion, achievements and all. Overall a beautiful game <3

This game is so cute, i got really emotional bringing some characters to the afterlife cause i just didn't want them to leave! the gameplay is really relaxing and comfortable to play, would definitely play again <3

This game is a true Masterpiece! If you like farming, upgrading buildings, lovable characters and discovering their stories, this game is just made for you. Most of the time it is really cozy and relaxing, especially later in the game. The music is beautiful and the artstyle is very cute.
In the beginning it is a bit mysterious what is happening wuth you, but over the course of theT game, more and more is revealed. What started out as a simple story became complex and deep. I highly advise talking a lot to your passengers to learn more about their life and their background.

Highly reccomend this game. 10/10 and you can hug your cat any time you want :)

I had a hard time writing this review because I did not manage to finish the game, But i just couldn't. Nothing is glaringly wrong with this game but it's...just not fun...It starts out a tad fun, with the need to explore and learn more pushing you forward adequately enough, But the core game loop becomes a very large chore very fast, to the point that I just didn't want to do it everyday. I failed to feel the connection to the characters that everyone else in the reviews was so excited about, and I wasn't saddened by their departure, If anything I was pleased to no have to support them anymore, despite my best efforts to connect to them, any many of them I felt i knew nothing about after their dialogues, I knew a lot about one very important aspect of their life, but that was it...except Atul, everyone loves Atul. I never intended to stop playing but I closed it out one night and never managed to open it again, and I doubt i will at this point, but maybe ill get the motivation again. Maybe you will get more enjoyment out of this then me, but understand it is a long game, with very little happening for the vast majority of it, with capturing moments throughout, Soundtrack 10/10 though, also appreciated fishing.
I was stuck a lot. It s a good game. Frustrated me a lil in some gameplay.

I started this game on PC then switched to console to finish and replay the game. My first play through topped off around 50 hours to get full completion. I absolutely adore this game, and it's story. I am still looking for a game to replace Spiritfarer and the comfort it brings me. Between the story, graphics, and soundtrack, this is by far my favorite game i've played.

This game can feel a little tedious at times but in an intentional way. It forces players to slow down and use critical thinking skills but will prompt users when they hit a dead end. It is an emotional game at times.
Gut-wrenchingly beautiful on all accounts, emotionally, visually, musically and without sacrificing the gameplay quality at any point. This is truly one of the best games I have ever played.

Very good game, very pretty, im really enjoying it, there seems to be a bug in the game where you have to take gwen to the everdoor and it makes me cry like a little bitch, see about getting that fixxed

Lovely game with a great message and you can see that a lot of love went into it. A lot of the characters also represent people the dev team personally knew who passed away and that puts it so much closer to the heart.
I often found myself with a heavy heart as I could feel the end of a character coming and enjoying every last interaction I had with them. Despite the sad undertone, I was quite content, even happy when I found out their favourite dishes by accident or upgraded their house fully...

It is wonderful experience :)

After almost 15 hours i finally finished my first Everdoor quest, after Gwen moved on past that door and i hugged her and went through the whole memories sequence i kept on playing for 30ish minutes before shutting it down and taking a break. That was an hour ago, i just realised there is no way il be able to go through that experience over and over again, im too young for this shit. So i uninstalled the game, i am sorry. 10/10 game, would highly recommend to anyone stronger than me, preferably someone who doesnt have a lot of childhood trauma from abuse, neglect and abandonment so they wont be affected as much.

Such a beautiful game with amazing art. Has characters that make you laugh and characters that make you cry. It has such a deeper meaning than I thought and get's you heartbroken as you get close to finishing it. Very very worth it.
Wish I was dedicated enough to finish the game, the characters are really sweet. Max level cozy game for sure. Also the cat is AMAZING!!!!

the art style is adorable, its such a relaxing game to play and i immediately found myself sucked into the story.
i've found myself laughing and crying while playing this game and honestly, i love it when i can get emotionally invested in a game without worrying about it effecting my mental health negatively.
i honestly would recommend this game to anyone that just wants something relaxing and cute to play, currently my favourite game. :D
Before i played this game i struggled with erectile dysfunction, had no life partner and little to no will to live. After i played, nothing changed, but the game was great.
☻☻☻☻ Great art, music, and interesting characters. Gameplay made me want to peel my eyeballs out with a spoon. Everything is unnecessarily slow, tedious, and repetitive. ☻☻☻☻
Haven't played too much, but I can already tell it's pretty great. Gameplay is really chill and simple, but the characters are the real strong suit. It's extremely bitter sweet, but it's fun.

What a beautiful game. Played the whole experience in couch co-op. Spent so much time not wanting to end the game, so did a fairly completionist-ish run.

There were definitely some moments we got a bit stuck and frustrated from how grindy the game got, but we just put it away for a while and came back later. This game isn't designed to be completed in a single setting, just a bit every now and then, and it feels best to take it at a slow pace.

It's a beautiful game. A very sad one, but also a cozy one. Definitely one of the best couch co-op games I have ever played, but be prepared to cry several times. Especially Stanley and Jackie hit me hard.

Bug sidenote:
Only really ran into a single annoying bug: hugging spirits (the blue coloured ones) as Daffodil can lock up the game for player 2 (but this is quite minor and you can just save and quit and reload with 0 progress loss).

Amazing game!! so pretty and perfect to play with a partner or friend C:

cutsie but emotional

This has almost immediately become one of my favorite games of all time. It's beautiful and cleverly written, but also really fun and engaging. It strikes a perfect balance in terms of challenge for a cozy game--not too hard, not too easy, not too grind-y. I 100% recommend it.

This game is a work of art. The art is beautiful, the characters are interesting, and the music is great. The game play is very relaxing but not boring, and it has a nice way of giving you things to do in order to progress without being pushy. I just finished it and I have to say, when you finish it leaves you with a very interesting feeling. It feels good to know that you've helped complete all these spirits last wishes, yet leaves a tint of sadness, after all those goodbyes, and seeing the ship slowly get emptier and emptier. The main story and subject is something that I will leave for you to experience in the game itself, but I will just leave you with the knowledge that it is very worth your $30, and you will almost certainly enjoy it.

its hard for me to talk about how much i care about this game, because i feel like words don't do it justice. i first found the game originally through gamepass in 2020, and fell in love with the art, music, and story right away. getting to know each of the spirits in the game, it feels like you're really connecting with them. they're people with big personalities, dreams, and flaws too, and when it's time to say goodbye, you don't want to let go. it's made me cry a lot, it's made me laugh a lot, and it's made me sit back and take in the beauty. most of all though, it's taught me that its okay to say goodbye.

Spiritfarer is a beautiful and fantastic game, lovely and heart-wrenching and fun from start to finish.

The art is gorgeous, the gameplay loop is very enticing and enjoyable, and the characters and their stories are excellently written.

While this is a wonderful game, it also centers around themes of loss, grief, fulfillment, and letting go. I recommend it to just about everyone, but take care of yourself and keep in mind that it's very emotional.

Interesting premise and a concept which is okay, feeling inspired by something like Ori with its big moments and events clad in moving music. But unfortunately the game is too long for its own good and the pacing can get messed up by the characters which where added after the initial release. Some of them are cool, like Gustav or the frog, whose name I already forgot.

This made me end up not really caring much about the characters I had left on my boat or at Overbrook and kind of rush towards the ending, just to finish it after playing for about 20 hours.

Çizimleri 90'lar çizgi filmlerinden fırlamış gibi olan bu tatlı oyunda bir gemi kaptanı olarak ordan oraya seyahat edip gemimize misafirler alıyoruz. Oyunun animasyonları son derece akıcı ve rahat. Müzikler, oynanış, grafikler her şey olması gerektiği gibi. Oyunda ilerledikçe oyunun sizi yönlendirmeyi bırakması, neyi nasıl yapacağınızı çözmekte sorun yaşamanız ve gemiyle seyahat etmenin biraz hantal olması haricinde çok gözüme çarpan bir eksisi yok. Sırf çizimleri için bile deneyim edilebilir. Gayet sakin, tatlı bir oyun.

I can't recommend this game enough. I lost a close friend and father figure to cancer; it was a brutal, slow death, and I wasn't able to process it because I had to take care of other people in my life. I wasn't suicidal because of Chip's death, but it exacerbated my depression, OCD, and suicidal tendencies - everything got so much worse after he was gone. Spiritfarer is a game about processing grief. It's a game about loving and knowing to let go. Please play it. Bring tissues <3

Such a beautiful game, I picked it up several years ago (around 2021 maybe?) and at the time it was great, definitely still is. The story is truly wonderful, brought me to tears during some quest lines for certain.
I took my time with it, because Spiritfarer can be a little overwhelming at times with the amount of things to do, stuff to interact with and things to collect that it becomes super hectic.
So if you're reading reviews and debating getting the game, get it! Just be mindful to take your time and enjoy it, because you'll likely get burnt out quick near the beginning-middle part when you're collecting.
All in all, a fantastic game that I was overjoyed to complete, it's absolutely worth the money!
Simple mechanics and a calming game, yet contains surprisingly rich character backstories if one stops to contemplate their true depth.
Amazing gameplay; love all of the different characters and their unique personalities. Wonderful graphics, every shot makes me amazed at what they have done.

You'll cry.
You'll ugly cry.
But...
it's worth it.

Aside from that, I'm not normally a big fan of resource management and getting caught up in farming - but this was lovely. It introduced new features at a great cadence. The explanations were fluid and meshed with the story line.

The artwork is beautiful.
The music is lovely.

Did I mention that you'll cry?

I just finished it and should have had tissues on hand. Silly mistake.

Absolutely play it, but pace yourself if you need to. <3
Ugh this game goes soooooo good and the mechanics art and story are exquisite and extremely satisfying

great for simple cozy playing, all the quests are super easy and just a google search away if needed :) but there is parkour so if ur dooky like me at parkour it might take ya 30 minutes to get to certain places LOL, super funs tho!!! ( ⸝⸝´ ᵕ `⸝⸝)

I loved this game. Everything from the platformer mechanics, the mini games, the music, and especially the emotional notes it hits is perfect. Every companion has an interesting story to share and lessons to learn and the area to explore has enough to do to keep you occupied for a long time. Recommended for people who love emotional depth and gorgeous music and excellent gameplay.

This game feels like a warm embrace with the cozy art style, beautiful soundscape and mostly the characters you grow into during your journey. This lovely little world warmed my heart. Sure, the story behind each characters takes some time to untangle and you have to do a lot of grinding to improve your boat and advance in every story. Maybe some of the grinding that the player is encouraged to do feels a little unnecessary, given that you get very little in return. For example, gathering stuff for errands. I still enjoyed every bit of my time. There is a lot to do and explore in and outside of the boat.

It is cute that every character has an impact on your progress in a way, and the characters are even inspired by real people. Playing Spiritfarer was a touching journey about life and what you leave behind after you leave. The characters never actually feel forgotten within time, which I really like in this game.

Ok, this game teaches a thing or two about living.

I'm usually a completionist, and I couldn't finish it 100% because I was so overwhelmed that I felt my journey was over.

I loved every single second of it. And I can't stop crying.
This is a very deep and emotional story told with light hearted mechanics and journeys.
A fun farming sim game, but it does reach a point where you are kind of overflowing with stuff and have nothing to use it for or on. Still it was a very enjoyable and surprisingly moving game.
Simply beautiful and relaxing with charming characters. Makes recovering from Covid-19 more bearable. Worth full price.

This game is absolutely gorgeous. To me it's easy to replay because the things these spirits say can help change the way I think. Not only that but if you're a completionist (i mean in terms of achievements) it's impossible to do so without playing the game more than once. It's a lot of fun to 100% this game, and I've played it twice already and have started a 3rd playthrough. It's interesting to see what changes when you know what you're doing.

tldr.text: Very Positive (95%): players praise the story, the characters and the art.
The main complaint is that quests and dialogue feel repetitive and boring.

details.text: Recent reviews are 97% positive, about the same as the all-time score, so the overall picture has held steady.
Players who have just started are 73% positive, while long-time players are 98% positive.
